S26.01.needs: a chat that produces an artifact
S26.01.note: The Code line pointed at InlineArtifactCards.tsx; the card itself is rendered by ArtifactCard.tsx, which I read directly.
steps: Sign in and start a new chat.
Ask for a short HTML page or a document so the reply produces an artifact.
Find the card in the reply that shows the artifact title and the type.
Click the card's "Open" button.
Look: the artifact opens in the panel and shows the content, as Expected.
S26.01.where: Chat > ask for a document or an HTML page > in the assistant's reply click the card's "Open" button

S26.02.needs: a chat that produces an artifact
S26.02.note: The fallback the viewer shows is "Artifact" and the card and list use "Untitled"; I did not find a control to force an untitled artifact.
steps: Ask for an artifact and click its card's "Open" button.
Read the title shown at the top of the viewer.
Find the same title on the card in the reply.
Make a second artifact with no title if the model gives one; check that the fallback shows "Untitled" in the list.
S26.02.where: Chat > open an artifact > read the title at the top of the viewer header

S26.03.needs: a chat that produces an artifact
S26.03.note: Card subtitle shows "Artifact" for runs-as-artifact cards and the type label otherwise, as read in ArtifactCard.tsx; the exact subtitle depends on the artifact.
steps: Ask for an HTML page, then a document, in separate replies.
Click "Open" on each card.
Read the grey line under each title: it shows the kind, for example "HTML" or "MD".
Compare the kind shown with the artifact that was made.
S26.03.where: Chat > open an artifact > read the grey line under the title in the viewer, and the line under the title on the card

S26.04.needs: a chat that produces a long artifact, and a way to stop the reply
S26.04.note: No visible word for finished or failed was found in the artifact files; the stopped notice text is 'This artifact was saved from a partial response. It may not include later output.' in ArtifactPreview.tsx.
steps: Ask for a long document or page and watch the Artifacts panel while the reply is still running.
Read the status text: it shows "Writing…" while content arrives.
Stop the reply (the stop control in the composer) while it is still writing.
Open that artifact and read the notice that says it was saved from a partial response.
Note: I did not find visible words for a finished or a failed state, so compare with Expected and report what you see.
S26.04.where: Chat > ask for a long artifact > watch the status text in the panel while it is written; the stopped state appears as a notice in the viewer

S26.05.needs: a chat that produces an artifact
steps: In a chat with an artifact, click the card's "Open" button.
Check that the viewer shows the artifact content.
Close the panel, click the Artifacts icon button (aria label "Open artifacts panel"), then click the artifact's tab.
Look: the same content is shown.
S26.05.where: Chat > click the card's "Open" button, or click the Artifacts icon button (aria label "Open artifacts panel") then pick the artifact tab

S26.06.needs: a chat that produces an artifact
steps: Open an artifact so the Artifacts panel shows it.
Click the X button labelled "Close artifact viewer" in the viewer header.
Look: the viewer hides.
Click the Artifacts icon button (aria label "Open artifacts panel") and check that the artifact is still listed as a tab or card.
S26.06.where: Artifacts panel > click the X button (aria label "Close artifacts panel") or the X in the viewer header (aria label "Close artifact viewer")

S26.07.needs: a chat that produces an artifact
S26.07.note: I read the code for reopening but did not check persistence after a reload.
steps: Open an artifact, then close the panel as in S26.06.
Click the Artifacts icon button (aria label "Open artifacts panel"), or go back to the chat and click the card's "Open" button.
Look: the same artifact opens.
Reload the page, then open the Artifacts panel again and check the artifact is still there.
S26.07.where: Chat > click the Artifacts icon button (aria label "Open artifacts panel") or the card's "Open" button

S26.08.note: Below 640 px the code shows the panel as an overlay instead of a docked side panel.
steps: Use a window wider than 639 px (the mobile overlay starts at 639 px or less).
Open an artifact from its card.
Look: the conversation and the Artifacts panel are both visible side by side.
Scroll the conversation and check the panel stays open.
S26.08.where: Chat in a wide window > open an artifact > the "Artifacts" panel docks on the right of the conversation

S26.09.needs: a desktop-width window and a mouse or keyboard
S26.09.note: The code for keeping the width after reopening was not read in this pass; the store is packages/ui/unified-chat/src/stores/uiStore.ts.
steps: Open an artifact so the docked panel is visible.
Drag the edge of the panel by its resize handle, or click the handle and press the Left or Right arrow key.
Look: the panel gets wider or narrower and the conversation resizes to match.
Close the panel, open it again, and check the width is kept.
S26.09.where: Artifacts panel (docked) > drag the thin handle labelled "Resize artifacts panel" or focus it and press the Left or Right arrow key

S26.10.needs: a chat that produces an artifact
steps: Open an artifact in the viewer.
Hover the header button titled "Expand" to see its tooltip.
Click it: the artifact fills the screen.
Click the "Exit fullscreen" button to return.
S26.10.where: Artifact viewer header > click the button labelled "Enter fullscreen" (title "Expand") > click it again labelled "Exit fullscreen"

S26.11.needs: a chat that produces an HTML or other renderable artifact
S26.11.note: The page is opened as a sandboxed blob in a new tab; a separate native window was not found in the code.
steps: Open a renderable artifact such as an HTML page.
Click the "More artifact actions" button (three dots).
Click "Open in new tab".
Look: a new browser tab opens and shows the rendered artifact.
S26.11.where: Artifact viewer > click "More artifact actions" > click "Open in new tab"

S26.12.note: The label on the second cards list is built from a template; the tab itself shows the artifact's own title.
steps: Make a conversation that produces at least two artifacts.
Open the Artifacts panel from the Artifacts icon button.
Click the tab for the second artifact by its title.
Look: the viewer changes to the second artifact without closing the panel.
Click the first tab and check it switches back.
S26.12.where: Chat with two or more artifacts > open the Artifacts panel > click a different artifact tab by its title

S26.13.needs: a chat where an artifact is being written
steps: Start a reply that writes an artifact.
Look at the tab row at the top of the Artifacts panel while it is written.
Look: the artifact being written has its own tab with a pulsing dot.
When it finishes, check it is still one tab, not two.
S26.13.where: Artifacts panel > tab row at the top (one tab per artifact); the artifact being written shows a pulsing dot in its tab

S26.14.needs: a chat that produces a renderable artifact
S26.14.note: The two icons appear only for renderable types.
steps: Open an HTML or other renderable artifact.
Click the eye icon labelled "Preview": the rendered page shows.
Click the code icon labelled "Source": the source code shows.
Look: the same artifact is shown in both modes.
S26.14.where: Artifact viewer header > the eye icon labelled "Preview" and the code icon labelled "Source"

S26.15.needs: a chat that produces an editable artifact
S26.15.note: The header Edit button is shown only for document-type artifacts in the code read; code artifacts use the "Edit source" menu item.
steps: Open an editable artifact such as a document.
Click the "Edit" button in the header.
Change some text in the editor.
Click the button titled "Save as a new version".
Look: a new version appears in the version chip (v2/…) and the new text shows.
S26.15.where: Artifact viewer > click the "Edit" button (for a document) or "More artifact actions" > "Edit source" (for code) > change the text > click "Save" (title "Save as a new version")

S26.16.needs: an artifact with at least two versions
S26.16.note: I read the read-only logic but did not confirm the exact hiding condition; check it against the older version behaviour before trusting this step.
steps: Open an artifact that has at least two versions.
Click the "Previous version" arrow to go to an older version.
Look: the Edit button and the Save controls are not shown for the older version.
S26.16.where: Shown as a missing Edit button when you step to an older version with "Previous version"

steps: Open an artifact with several versions.
Look at the chip under the title: it shows the current version as "v N/M".
Click the "Version history" chip.
Click another version in the list.
Look: the viewer shows that version and the chip number changes.
S26.20.where: Artifact viewer > click the version chip "v2/3" under the title (its tooltip is "Version history") > choose another version in the list

steps: Open an artifact with several versions.
Click the "Previous version" arrow: an older version shows.
Read the "v N/M" number to see which version is shown.
Click the "Next version" arrow to step forward again.
S26.21.where: Artifact viewer > the left arrow "Previous version" and right arrow "Next version" on either side of the "v N/M" chip under the title

S26.23.needs: an artifact with at least three versions
steps: Open an artifact with at least three versions.
Click the "Version history" chip and pick an earlier version.
Click "Restore" for that version, then confirm in the dialog that asks "Restore version N?".
Look: the restored version is now the current one.
Open the version history again and check the newer versions are still listed.
S26.23.where: Artifact viewer > click the "Version history" chip under the title > click "Restore" beside an earlier version > confirm "Restore"

S26.24.needs: a saved artifact in the Artifacts panel
S26.24.note: The Duplicate item appears only in the panel variant for stored artifacts.
steps: Open a saved artifact in the Artifacts panel (panel view, not the inline card).
Click "More artifact actions" and click "Duplicate".
Look: the toast says "Duplicated. Edits here no longer touch the original."
Edit the copy, then open the original and check it did not change.
S26.24.where: Artifacts panel > open a saved artifact > click "More artifact actions" > click "Duplicate"

S26.26.needs: a signed-in account with a Library
S26.26.note: I did not find the sidebar word for the Library; check the Library location in the app before the test.
steps: Open a saved artifact that is not a generated file, image, PDF or Word document.
Click "More artifact actions" and click "Save to Library".
Look: the toast says "Saved to your Library".
Open your Library and find the artifact there.
S26.26.where: Artifact viewer > click "More artifact actions" > click "Save to Library"

S26.27.note: The project list is only shown when the account has projects.
steps: Make sure the account has at least one project.
Open an artifact and click "More artifact actions".
Under "Save to project", click a project name.
Look: a bar with "In project" and the project link appears under the header.
Open that project and check the artifact is listed.
S26.27.where: Artifact viewer > click "More artifact actions" > under the group "Save to project" click a project name > look for "In project" under the header

S26.28.needs: a saved artifact in the Library
S26.28.note: The Library's Add to chat uses the file, not a live artifact link. The Start Work item in the viewer's More menu is a different action; the Library's label for the item menu was not confirmed.
steps: Open the Library and find a saved artifact item.
Click "Add to chat".
Look: a new chat opens with the item attached.
Ask for a change to it and check the reply continues from that content.
S26.28.where: Library > open an artifact item > click "Add to chat"

S26.29.needs: an artifact with several export formats
S26.29.note: When only one format exists, the download icon saves directly with no menu; the format list depends on artifact type.
steps: Open an artifact that has more than one download format (for example a document).
Click the download icon in the header.
Look: a menu lists formats such as "Download as Markdown" or "Download as PDF".
Pick one and check the file is saved in that format.
S26.29.where: Artifact viewer > click the download icon (title "Download") > choose a format such as "Download as Markdown"

S26.30.needs: a text, code or document artifact
S26.30.note: The copy button is hidden for PDF, Word and image artifacts.
steps: Open a text, code or document artifact.
Click the "Copy" button in the header.
Look: the button changes to a check mark and the word "Copied".
Paste into a text field and compare with the artifact content.
S26.30.where: Artifact viewer > click the copy icon labelled "Copy" (aria label "Copy artifact") in the header

S26.31.needs: a signed-in account; a Free or paid account; a workspace is needed only for the 'Everyone in this workspace' option
S26.31.note: No 'take down' or 'unpublish' control found for an artifact. The only revoke wording is 'Revoke share' in apps/web/features/chat/components/share/ShareConversationDialog.tsx, which is for whole chats. Searched for unpublish, take down, stop sharing, remove link in the artifacts folders.
steps: Sign in and open a chat that has an artifact, then click its card to open the viewer.
Click the 'Publish' button in the viewer header (or 'Share' icon, title 'Share').
Check the link bar appears with 'Copy link' and the 'Who can open this' dropdown; click 'Copy link' and look for 'Link copied'.
Open the 'Who can open this' dropdown and pick another option; compare with Expected: choose who can open the link.
S26.31.where: Chat > open an artifact card > artifact viewer header: Publish, Copy link, Who can open this

S26.32.needs: a signed-in account; a workspace member count is needed to show 'Everyone in this workspace'
S26.32.note: No separate private/public badge was found on the artifact card or list; the state shows only as the dropdown after publishing. The unpublished (private) state has no label found.
steps: Open a published artifact in the viewer (click 'Publish' first if it is not yet published).
Look at the link bar under the header for the 'Who can open this' dropdown and its current choice.
Open the dropdown and compare the three choices with Expected: private, anyone with the link, or workspace.
S26.32.where: Chat > open an artifact card > Publish > 'Who can open this' dropdown

S26.35.needs: a Free or paid account; an artifact that fails at run time
S26.35.note: The sandbox only shows the error message in a plain pre block. No source or retry control was found in infrastructure/sandbox/index.html or ArtifactPreview.tsx, so Expected's buttons are unconfirmed.
steps: Open an artifact whose code throws an error when it runs.
Look in the preview for the red-text block starting with 'Render error:'.
Compare with Expected: the viewer shows an error panel that explains the failure and offers source or retry.
S26.35.where: Chat > open an HTML or React artifact that fails when it runs > preview area shows the error text

S26.36.needs: a Free or paid account; a slow or offline connection helps to see the state
S26.36.note: Only the React loading text was found. The failed-load report is in the sandbox as an error message, and it was not verified as visible to the user.
steps: Open a React artifact in the viewer.
Look at the preview area while it starts; the text 'Loading React…' shows until the runtime loads.
Compare with Expected: loading state shown, and a failed load reported.
S26.36.where: Chat > open a React artifact > preview area while the libraries load

S26.38.needs: a signed-in account with at least one artifact in the gallery
S26.38.note: No 'Gallery' item was found in the sidebar menu. The same 'Open chat' label also exists in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/library/LibraryView.tsx for the Library path.
steps: Open the gallery page at /gallery.
Click an artifact to open its drawer.
Click the 'Open chat' link in the drawer.
Compare with Expected: the chat that made the artifact opens.
S26.38.where: Gallery page (web address /gallery) > open an artifact card > Open chat

S26.39.needs: a Free or paid account; a model reply that produces an artifact
steps: Send a request that asks for an artifact, and click its card while the reply is still running.
Watch the viewer header for the 'Writing…' label with a pulsing dot.
Watch the content area for it to grow while the reply streams.
Compare with Expected: content appears live until the reply ends.
S26.39.where: Chat > send a request that makes an artifact > click the artifact card while it is being written

S26.40.note: The rule is a media query, (max-width: 639px), in apps/web/features/chat/stores/artifacts-store.ts; the effect is seen as an overlay. Touch controls were not verified in the code.
steps: Open a chat with an artifact on a phone-sized browser window (640 px wide or less) or on a phone.
Click the artifact card and check that the viewer covers the screen as an overlay, not a docked side panel.
Compare with Expected: full-screen reader with touch controls.
S26.40.where: Phone-width screen: the artifact opens as an overlay sheet instead of a side panel
